body.estimand_functional: \(R_{XY}(p)=\Pr_p\{P_x(y)\text{ is identifiable in }G_Z\}=\sum_{S:\operatorname{Fail}(S)=0}\prod_{e\in S}p_e\prod_{e\notin S}(1-p_e),\quad p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent Bernoulli realization of uncertain directed and bidirected edges in a fixed topologically ordered ADMG envelope.
sampling_model.units: The finite vertices \(V\) are fixed; there is no sampling of observational units in the theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention set \(X\) and outcome set \(Y\) are fixed before the edge realization.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the real probabilities \(p_e\in[0,1]\) encode structural uncertainty rather than treatment assignment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; \(p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\) and the envelope are computational inputs. Rational coordinates are required only when the exact bit-complexity guarantee is invoked, and no calibration claim for estimated edge probabilities is made.
sampling_model.randomness: Only \(Z\) is random, with mutually independent coordinates.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The edge ID problem is NP-complete.
Lemma 7 states that Algorithm 2 returns an optimal solution to the minimum-cost intervention problem in Equation (2).
We can enumerate all minimal directed Steiner trees in \(O(nm)\) delay and \(O(n+m)\) space.
The minimal transversals can be enumerated in fixed-parameter-linear delay following an FPT preprocessing phase.
Our algorithm runs in time \(O(4^k k\ell N)\).
Source--sink reliability is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete even for acyclic directed planar graphs having vertex degree at most three.
The ID algorithm is complete for identification of interventional distributions in semi-Markovian causal models.
Proposition 1 states that the ID algorithm fails exactly when a hedge exists for the original identification query.
The directed path-conjunction special case admits polynomial-delay enumeration.
Project--join trees support exact weighted model counting by dynamic programming.
Network reliability is fixed-parameter tractable for bounded-treewidth networks.
Counting vertex covers in bipartite graphs is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete.

body.tldr: A probabilistic ADMG currently yields one high-plausibility identifiable realization, not the total chance that a fixed causal query is identifiable or the minimal edge combinations that destroy it. The proposal makes those combinations the hyperedges of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), compresses every hedge into a \(2b-2\)-edge core plus directed ancestry obligations, and targets a canonical \(2^{O(b\log b)}\)-delay compiler. The full \(b\le2\) class is handled by a formally labelled transition DAG; a deterministic-diamond instance shows that distinct deterministic paths yield one uncertain-edge support and one output. Once the new compiler makes \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) explicit, standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on an incidence decomposition yields reliability and all edge sensitivities as an implementation corollary, while a width-two causal reduction proves that exact successful-realization counting remains \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete.

project_justification.gap: Ordinary ID certifies failure in one ADMG by a hedge, and edgeID chooses one plausible identifiable subgraph, but neither theory enumerates the globally minimal uncertain-edge causes of failure across all realizations.
project_justification.niche: Maximum envelope district size bounds the local bidirected and forest part of every hedge without bounding its directed ancestry paths. This exposes a parameterized enumeration problem that is causal in its core and combinatorial in its unbounded remainder.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sparse-core representation, a canonical duplicate-free compiler with a complete width-two construction, a standard weighted-model-counting implementation corollary for the compiled output, and a sharp width-two causal counting-complexity boundary.

body.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl (2008) establish soundness and completeness of ordinary ID through hedge certificates; Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1, \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2307.03750\)) gives the corrected equivalence between ID failure and a hedge for the original query. These results supply the causal equivalence used here, not support-enumeration results. Akbari et al. (2023) formulate probabilistic ADMGs and prove edge ID is NP-complete, but their objective selects one edge-deleted identifiable graph. In the final JMLR article, Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025, Definition 6 and Algorithm 2 on pages 10--12, with optimality in Lemma 7) define vertex-minimal hedges, iteratively discover only enough such hedges to solve a minimum hitting-set intervention problem, and explicitly avoid enumerating all hedges. That machinery optimizes interventions in one fixed graph; it neither enumerates uncertain-edge-minimal supports for failure of the original query nor proves output-sensitive delay under deterministic-path projection and cross-core domination. Khachiyan et al. (2007) and Kobayashi, Kurita, and Wasa (2022) provide path and directed-Steiner enumeration techniques, but their selected-edge witnesses do not identify deterministic paths that collapse to the same uncertain support. Kenig and Mizrahi (2025) obtain fixed-parameter-linear delay for minimal transversals when an explicit incidence decomposition is supplied, whereas this project must first compile an implicit causal obstruction hypergraph under parameter \(b\). Samer and Szeider (2010) supply standard exact CNF model counting at bounded incidence treewidth, and Dudek, Phan, and Vardi (2020) supply standard literal-weighted project--join dynamic programming. The reliability and full-gradient computations here are an implementation consequence of those generic methods after the new causal compiler emits \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), not an independently novel dynamic program. Goharshady and Mohammadi (2020) compute classical network reliability at bounded network treewidth and further confirm that the counting component belongs to established reliability methodology. Provan (1986) and Provan and Ball (1983) supply the counting-hardness sources for the width-preserving causal reduction.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A completed minimal ancestry support gives each uncertain edge a private root and orders that root's mandatory edges as dominators, but the private-root assignment has not been proved stable for partial supports. Distinct cores may yield the same completion or a strict superset of another completion. The general delay theorem therefore cannot be obtained by enumerating path witnesses and filtering: deterministic diamonds create exponentially many witnesses for one uncertain support, and post-output filtering does not bound exhaustion delay.
body.honest_scope: The sparse-core reduction, the complete \(b\le2\) labelled-transition-DAG algorithm, and the width-two counting reduction are theorem targets, not established results. The reliability identity, full-gradient formula, and incidence-treewidth computation are explicitly implementation propositions obtained from the compiled obstruction hypergraph by standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting and project--join dynamic programming; they are not claimed as an independent algorithmic novelty. The deterministic-diamond proposition is a worked projection and duplicate-suppression check, not a substitute for the general width-two proof. The root-ordered partial-support recursion for general \(b\) is the open kernel. Its first kill test is exhaustive comparison with brute-force minimal supports on all specified envelopes with at most six vertices, \(b\le3\), and at most eight uncertain edges; any missing support, duplicate, false live branch, or loss of global minimality rejects the state design. No claim is made that the edge probabilities are calibrated, that one identifying formula is common to all successful realizations, or that \(b\) controls total output size.
